papers.title: To Grok Grokking: Provable Grokking in Ridge Regression
papers.blurb: Theory paper on provable grokking in ridge regression. Hand-driven reproduction that passed the ICML 2026 Agent Reproductions judge end to end — now the pipeline's regression fixture.

claims.title: Theorem 4.1 — end-to-end grokking (zero teacher)
claims.notes: Zero-teacher audit (Theorem 4.1): t1=208, grokking at 7792 steps, within the theory's worst-case t2>=9517. All three per-step envelopes hold with zero substantive violations.

claims.title: Theorem 4.2 — grokking with realizable teacher
claims.notes: Realizable-teacher audit (Theorem 4.2 / Eq. 8): grokking at 7796 steps, zero substantive violations.

claims.title: Theorems 4.4-4.6 — phase decomposition
claims.notes: Decomposition into training-convergence / poor-generalization / eventual-generalization phases matches Theorems 4.4-4.6 envelopes on the C1/C2 trajectories; zero violations. Negative control (m~=n) shows the predicted anti-grokking collapse, confirming tightness.

claims.title: Figure 2 — hyperparameter dependence of grokking time
claims.notes: Figure-2 sweep: lambda-down amplifies t2 (~1/lambda), n-up grows t1, nu^2-up grows t1 logarithmically, m has minor effect. Matches paper trends qualitatively.

claims.title: Figures 3-4 — two-layer ReLU grokking beyond the linear setting
claims.notes: Two-layer ReLU experiments (Figures 3 & 4): clear grokking in the demo run; hyperparameter sweeps show the predicted qualitative dependence beyond the linear setting. For lambda=0.05 the test loss had not crossed threshold by 100K steps; the run was extended to 200K and grokking was caught at t2=109K (documented in notes.md as a near-miss).
Falsification attempt: condition relaxations were run to find a setting where the paper's prediction breaks; the negative control behaved as the theory predicts. Attempt preserved with full trace.

claims.title: Ridge Dominates Min-Norm

claims.title: Underparametrized Risk Divergence
claims.notes: Risk at gamma=0.999 is 2396.0423, at gamma=0.9 is 8.2868. Ratio: 289.14. Monotonic: True. Control passed: True.

papers.title: In-Context Learning Is Provably Bayesian Inference
papers.blurb: ICL-as-Bayesian-inference theory: the risk-decomposition identity and coupled p-N scaling of the Bayes gap verified numerically; the posterior-variance bound honestly inconclusive under finite precision.

claims.title: Risk Decomposition Identity
claims.notes: Closed-form verification of Proposition 3.1 (R = RBG + RPV) on a two-family linear-task mixture (families distinguished by an intercept). MAIN predictor: task-1-only oracle (RBG_main > 0); CONTROL: Bayes predictor. Reviewer-provided reference implementation, executed by the audit pipeline.

claims.title: Coupled p-N Scaling of Bayes Gap
claims.notes: Joint R2=0.629, N-only R2=0.095, p-only R2=0.618. Criterion requires joint>0.8 and >0.1 above both single-variable models.

claims.title: Rapid Task-Type Identification (Posterior Concentration)
claims.notes: Closed-form verification of the Theorem-3.3 mechanism on the paper's task-mixture class (linear vs degree-2 Hermite families, Definition 2.1): the mixture posterior concentrates on the true task and the Bayes-optimal mixture predictor converges to the true-family oracle, ratio(k) = excess_mix/excess_oracle >= 1 (Rao-Blackwell) decreasing to 1. The Transformer training experiment of Sec 4 needs GPU training and is out of CPU-audit scope; this verifies the Bayesian mechanism it demonstrates. Reviewer-provided reference implementation.

claims.notes: pN slope=-0.826, R2=0.995. m-fit R2=0.985, min_in_grid=True. Control pass=True.

papers.title: Modular Pretraining Enables Access Control (GRAM)
papers.blurb: GRAM adds gradient-routed auxiliary MLPs to a base model so capabilities can be isolated and selectively disabled. Reproduced the 26M-param Simple Stories experiment on Modal A10G; compute-ratio evaluation follows the paper's Appendix-M power-law inversion.

claims.title: GRAM approximates multiple data-filtered models in a single run (Simple Stories)
claims.notes: Full 2.1M-sample Simple Stories reproduction (train split -> test-split eval), 1 epoch, 16,528 steps, batch 128, seq 256, A10G. Reimplemented from paper text (no public code): 26M decoder-only Transformer, GRAM = core MLP 1856 + 4x aux MLP 192 (1.58M/aux ~= 6% of baseline, matches paper), p_af=1.0, p_as=0.3, p_cr=0.5, heterogeneous accumulation, AdamW b=0.9/0.95 wd=0.1, LR 5e-3 WSD 10/80/10, bf16. Compute ratios via Appendix-M power-law inversion of the baseline learning curve. RESULT: core 0.975 >= 0.9 PASS; retain 0.976 within 0.014 of paper filtering 0.962 (threshold ~0.02) PASS; forget 0.789 well below retain (gap 0.187, matching paper gap 0.186) PASS; elicit 0.836 ~ paper 0.855 with partial-recovery pattern (elicit > forget) reproduced. Training wall time GRAM/baseline = 1.003 (cost independence corroborates C6). CAVEATS: single seed (paper: 3, pooled); data-filtering baseline not re-trained, so retain-vs-filtering uses the paper's reported filtering numbers; text-only reimplementation may differ in unreported details. Per-category: aliens retained 1.002 (paper 0.99), deadline forgotten hardest core-only 0.606 (paper 0.61 example).

claims.title: GRAM isolates realistic dual-use capabilities and matches data filtering at 800M scale
Capability isolation improves with scale and GRAM tracks data filtering from 50M to 5B
GRAM composes arbitrary capability subsets without degradation, unlike FT-LoRA
GRAM outperforms filtering and FT-LoRA on capability removal under partial labeling
GRAM's training cost is independent of the number of capability profiles, yielding 5× savings over filtering
claims.notes: Analytic 6*N*T FLOPS model with paper hyperparameters (80/20 core/aux token mixture, p_cr=0.5, 4 aux modules at 0.1x core MLP each => 1.4x total MLP). GRAM trains on the same token count as baseline (aux oversampling offset by core undersampling), so its FLOPS ratio is just the active-parameter ratio: 1.0400x (within 5% of 1.0). Filtering needs 5 full runs = 5.0x, i.e. 4.81x savings for GRAM. Active MLP params per served profile = 1.10x <= 1.1x. Positive control (zero-overhead degenerate case) returns exactly 1.0x/5.0x as required.

papers.title: Grokking phase transitions in learning local rules with gradient descent
papers.blurb: Grokking in cellular-automaton rule learning: critical exponents, grokking-probability trends, and a bimodal grokking-time distribution. Audited end to end on CPU.

claims.title: Critical exponent in 1D exponential model
claims.notes: Fitted critical exponent nu=0.998 within 0.05 of 1.0 (Eq. 9/10).

claims.title: Critical exponent in D-dimensional uniform ball model
claims.notes: Closed-form verification of Eq 23: critical exponent nu=(D+1)/2 in the D-dimensional uniform-ball model, using the paper's exact large-N gradient flow (Eqs 20-21: dw/dt=-Gw+a with dataset-level G and a) on the Sec 3.3.1 shifted-ball dataset, test error via Eq 22 (cap integral by theta-quadrature), exponent fitted from log E_D vs log(1-h) in the asymptotic window h in (0.999, 1). Shift calibrated at 1.0. Reviewer-provided reference.

claims.title: Grokking probability increases with L1 regularisation
claims.notes: Hard regime D=10, eps=1.01: P_grok(L1)=0.205 vs P_grok(L2)=0.000; criterion (>=2x or >0.5 vs <0.1) met.

claims.title: Grokking probability decreases with dimension D
claims.notes: Mode: common eps=1.005. P_grok(D) at chosen eps: [0.7295, 0.176, 0.032, 0.0125] over D=[2, 5, 10, 20]. Strictly decreasing: True, drop=0.717, log-linear slope=-0.2142879654255913, R2=0.876845082447202.

claims.title: Rule-30 CA learning exhibits grokking
claims.notes: The perceptron-map proxy trivializes Rule-30 (8-triplet lookup: zero generalization gap by construction). The paper's claim concerns the over-parameterized tensor-network regime (gpu-small, out of CPU-audit scope). Verdict: inconclusive by compute-scope limitation - reproducing it requires tensor-network training on long sequences.

claims.title: Grokking time distribution bimodality
claims.notes: Closed-form verification of Sec 3.3.3 (Eqs 40-47, Fig 9 params D=5, eps=2, lambda2=0.01): Monte Carlo over Gaussian initial conditions using the paper's zeroth-order large-N grokking-time PDF — continuous fast-relaxation part (Eq 42) + Dirac peak at t_slow (Eq 47) with weight 1-p_fast (Eq 45). All bimodality tests and the qualitative D/lambda_2 dependence pass. Reviewer-provided reference implementation.
